correctness.rationale: A strict Gaussian score ordering determines each Minkowski simplex winner. At cutoff 1, pairwise hub–leaf winners encode precisely the subset above the hub; at any cutoff at least 2, triple winners additionally encode the entire decreasing order of those leaves, and all larger winner decisions are functions of that list. Counting braid chambers gives exact cone angles and power sums. Uniform binomial-entropy and logarithmic factorial estimates yield the 1/n and 1/(n log n) crossover integrals, including the Shannon limit at zero. Endpoint dominance yields the exact asymptotic collision constants. All 21 cutoff/dimension cases through six leaves, comprising 34,406 strict rankings, were directly checked in the included standard-library checker. The finite checks are not used in place of proofs for arbitrary dimension.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The graph-associahedron and generalized-permutohedron normal-fan results cover the geometric family and can imply basic chamber counts. They do not themselves establish the quantified Rényi transition with n-dependent index and the two Riemann-integral limits; the latter are separately proved. This distinction prevents misidentifying an immediate fan corollary as standalone originality.

originality.rationale: The polytope family, stabilized star normal fan and partial-permutation vertex indexing are prior results, and elementary Gaussian chamber weights can be deduced from them. The selected distinct claim is the paired full Rényi-angular power-sum formulas and sharp contrast between the 1/n and 1/(n log n) critical windows, including their explicit crossover curves and collision-halving asymptotic. The inspected source text and targeted equivalence/coverage searches did not exhibit these quantitative statements. A bibliographically unindexed equivalent remains possible; a failed search is not proof of uniqueness.
residual_risks: A bibliographically unindexed entropy calculation under star elimination-tree, weak-order fan, or partial-permutation terminology could overlap.

value.rationale: The complete angular Rényi spectrum measures geometric exposure concentration for an infinite family of standard Euclidean graph polytopes. The first triangle-simplex refinement changes the order of Shannon entropy from n to n log n and the natural critical index scaling from 1/n to 1/(n log n), with explicit nonconstant crossover functions on both sides. The collision-halving limit gives a sharp operational consequence in independent random-direction vertex selection. This is a motivated complete quantitative classification rather than a low-dimensional arbitrary table or routine renaming.
